themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 150 THIS WEEK, a 660% spike versus the 8-week average of 19.8 weekly complaints (z-score: 18.03), signaling a sudden, severe deterioration in road surfaces across Forest Hills/Rego Park that demands immediate investigation into what triggered this crisis-level surge.
evidence: 150 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (660% increase)
Z-score of 18.03 indicates extremely rare statistical deviation, highest severity ranking
Street Condition is among top 10 complaint types by volume (543 total over 90 days), now acute
reporting_angles: Investigate what infrastructure failure or weather event triggered this week's surge—potholes, subsidence, water main breaks?
Interview residents about street hazards and impact on daily life; document specific locations with photos
Analyze DOE data on street resurfacing schedule and budget allocation to CD 406 vs. other districts

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal System Malfunction
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal complaints spiked to 86 LAST WEEK, a 347% jump from the 8-week average of 19.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.28), suggesting a widespread, sudden breakdown in signal infrastructure that poses safety and congestion risks across the district.
evidence: 86 traffic signal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 19.2 weekly average (347% spike, z-score: 8.28)
Traffic Signal Condition is in top 10 complaint types by volume (351 total over 90 days)
Spike occurred over single week, indicating acute rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to identify which signals failed and why—power outages, controller failures, weather damage?
Map complaint locations to identify if spike is geographically concentrated on major corridors (Queens Blvd, Yellowstone Blvd?)
Interview drivers and pedestrians about traffic jams and safety concerns caused by malfunctioning signals

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK, a 1233% spike from the 8-week average of 0.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.65), marking an unusual and sudden uptick that may indicate coordinated tagging activity or a breakdown in rapid removal protocols.
evidence: 5 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (1233% increase, z-score: 6.65)
Graffiti normally rare in this district (bottom of 311 complaint list), making spike statistically anomalous
Surge occurred over single week, suggesting new activity rather than delayed reporting
reporting_angles: Canvass neighborhoods for visual confirmation of graffiti hot spots; photograph and map locations
Interview NYPD and Sanitation about any known crews or coordinated tagging campaigns in the district
Compare timeline to recent community events or tensions that might explain sudden spike

themes_detail.label: Damaged Trees & Storm Damage
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints reached 30 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 674% spike from the 8-week average of 3.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.67), suggesting severe weather or pest damage that may still be affecting neighborhood aesthetics and safety.
evidence: 30 damaged tree complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.9 weekly average (674% increase, z-score: 6.67)
Aligns with Street Condition spike, suggesting weather event or environmental stressor affected infrastructure broadly
Parks Department budget requests (from CB file) include 'new or expanded park or amenity'—unmet need for tree maintenance?
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather (wind, ice) caused damage or if long-term neglect/pests are culprit
Request Parks Dept. tree removal and replacement data for CD 406 over past 12 months
Interview residents about tree canopy loss and request for faster removal of hazardous trees

themes_detail.label: School Facility Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: School maintenance complaints spiked to 8 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% jump from the 8-week average of 0.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 10.61), indicating a sudden, acute problem in school building conditions that affects student and staff safety or comfort.
evidence: 8 school maintenance complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 10.61)
School maintenance normally rare in district, making spike highly anomalous
Community Board budget requests include 'renovate or upgrade a senior center'—suggests broader facility maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Identify which schools filed complaints—reach out to principals and parents about specific maintenance issues
Request DOE capital budget data for CD 406 schools; compare to funding for other districts
Interview teachers and custodians about deferred maintenance affecting daily operations
